FADER (2018, on Virtual Self): described trying to recreate "what electronic music sounded like when I was 12 years old, just typing the word 'techno' into Limewire and downloading horribly mislabeled songs by Aphex Twin and other artists."

Geoff Barrow's own account (Mojo, 1999) of working as tape-op on Massive Attack's Blue Lines sessions in 1991; Massive Attack gave him spare studio time to develop his own ideas, directly leading to Portishead's formation. Corroborated by Far Out Magazine and Paste's Dummy at 30 retrospective.

Joe Strummer told Kris Needs in Louder (October 1976) that the Ramones' debut album was what made him join the band, and that he spent weeks learning to play along to it; he later told CNN he doubted London's punk scene could have been built without that record.
In the same Louder interview with Kris Needs (October 1976), Joe Strummer named seeing the Sex Pistols as the other formative event of that year, alongside discovering the Ramones' debut album.
Philip Oakey, Variety interview: "We loved Roxy Music and we loved David Bowie... They were the inspirations to us."
Montana Kaimin 2017, Mercer on what still shapes the records: bands he loved in high school -- Echo and the Bunnymen, the Cure, the Smiths.

Jim Ward called Sunny Day Real Estate "Fugazi beyond Fugazi" -- Wikipedia-mediated quote, flagged weaker-tier.
Steve Albini named This Heat among the favorite regional and overseas bands that shaped him, in a 2020 interview with VWMusic.

Doug Martsch told Esquire in 2015 that Dinosaur Jr.'s You're Living All Over Me took him about ten listens before he liked it at all -- and then he loved it; he has called it the record that shaped both Treepeople and Built to Spill.
Far Out Magazine: Shelley and Devoto "knew all of them back to front" -- the Stooges and the Velvet Underground both -- well before Buzzcocks existed.

Dan Snaith, RBMA Daily ("Caribou on Singing, Love, and Vangelis," 2014): "The first record that I made as Manitoba... was trying to sound like late '90s, early '00s Warp. It was influenced by Boards of Canada and Aphex Twin."
